presentations.more: `MIME` is a table of fixed entries, and this asks it about a key the code did not choose. Indexing answers "what does this name resolve to", which on an ordinary object includes everything the language put there before the author's own keys — so a key like `constructor` comes back with a value, and it is neither absent nor falsy. Testing the RESULT cannot separate the two cases; only asking whether the key is one of the table's OWN can. Use a presence test, or a map that holds only what was put in it.

This line reads through `manifest.base` as though the field were there, so any payload without it fails here with a null dereference instead of being rejected as malformed. Test for the field first, use an accessor that answers a default, or validate the payload against a schema before reading from it.

presentations.more: `manifest` is what a parser answered for text from outside the program, which nothing shows a caller cannot choose, and a parser answers whatever the text holds — an object, a list, a number or `null`. Nothing after the parse in this function checks that it is an object before it is used as one, in one place, named beside this one (the first on each path), so text of `null` — and, depending on the use, a number or a list — ends the request in an error there instead of being refused as malformed, and no handler takes the failure.
